children: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he had considered an "extreme tail risk" when asked whether he had seriously weighed the risk of U.S. military action against Canada. According to Sina Finance, Carney said in an interview that people in senior positions have a responsibility to focus on extreme tail risks, adding that it is "just risk management." He said a U.S. invasion was "not a baseline scenario," but that failing to prepare would be irresponsible.

In the wide-ranging interview, Carney outlined several steps Canada is taking to reduce its economic and strategic dependence on the United States. According to Sina Finance, he said Canada would seek to reduce its reliance on satellite broadband services provided by Elon Musk's SpaceX, adding that Canada would gradually reduce its dependence on Starlink.

Carney also said it would not make sense to break up the closely linked auto industry chain between the two countries, and he warned against using Canadian energy and food exports to the United States as bargaining chips. According to Sina Finance, he said he expects global demand for alternatives to the U.S. dollar to grow, partly because of the Trump administration's "pressure" tactics toward trading partners.

Carney said a global financial system that depends entirely on the U.S. dollar is unsustainable, and that a multipolar system with multiple reserve currencies would "provide greater flexibility." Despite the tensions, he told the newspaper that he and U.S. President Donald Trump speak "often," and that the two have communicated "many times" since trade talks broke down in August.

title: Canada's Carney Says U.S. Invasion Is an "Extreme Tail Risk"
